0030 — Select corpus repositories independently of results; target 200 per ecosystem

Status: proposed; accepted when the maintainer merges the pull request for #2116.

Problem

The corpus-tooling epic (#1993) targets 200 repositories per ecosystem, but earlier batches used different activity windows, size limits, and version-specific searches. Without a common rule, growth can favor familiar stacks or repositories Offing already handles well. A small ecosystem may not have 200 eligible projects.

This record defines selection policy for future growth. It does not relabel historical batches described in Validation corpus, implement discovery or labeling, or change detector maturity requirements in decision 0013.

Decision

1. Freeze eligibility before scanning

For each batch, commit the discovery date (UTC), queries, filters, ordered candidate list, selected repositories, skip reasons, and default-branch commit SHAs before running Offing on the selections. Preserve the search snapshot because live rankings change. Apply these rules equally to all ecosystems:

Criterion Rule for new blind selections
Public and independent Public, not archived, not a fork or mirror. Count one upstream project once; renamed repositories and duplicate pins are not new projects. No minimum stars, downloads, or organization membership.
Activity The default branch has a commit within the 24 calendar months ending on the recorded discovery date. Check the commit date, not issue activity or the repository's general update timestamp. Freeze this cutoff for the batch.
Size GitHub's reported repository size is at most 50,000 KB, following earlier corpus batches. Record the value at discovery; sparse checkout does not exempt an oversized repository.
License A license file at the selected commit grants use under an identified OSI-approved open-source license. Record its path and SPDX identifier; for multiple licenses, identify the one covering the inspected files. Missing, ambiguous, or incompatible coverage is a recorded skip pending human review, never assumed permission.
Ecosystem evidence The pinned tree contains at least one input form the ecosystem's detector documents reading. Inspect files as text only. A matching language tag alone is insufficient; no particular dependency version or finding is required.

Fetches belong to the separate corpus tooling. Scans remain offline; never install, build, execute repository code, run its scripts or tools, or evaluate its configuration to decide eligibility or labels. Store metadata, paths, line numbers, and minimal evidence quotations, not vendored repository contents; retain license notices when quoting evidence.

Existing pins remain reproducible historical regression evidence even if the project later becomes inactive, archived, or too large. Do not silently repin or retroactively call an old selection blind. Historical migration examples that do not meet the new blind-selection rules may be retained as explicitly targeted evidence, with their original selection rationale, and reported separately from eligible progress toward 200.

2. Cover all 23 ecosystem buckets

Use the existing corpus bucket names, including node for npm/Node.js and node-actions for GitHub Actions. The following table is the scope, including the three buckets with no entries at the time of this decision. The examples guide diversity; the detector documentation owns the exact supported input forms.

Bucket Stack or input variety to seek
android Java and Kotlin; Groovy and Kotlin Gradle builds
ci-images Azure Pipelines and GitHub Actions runner declarations
container Dockerfiles and Compose; single-stage and multi-stage images
cpp C and C++; CMake and supported dependency manifests
dart Dart packages and Flutter applications
database Compose and Terraform; different database engines and cloud providers
deno Deno and Bun; runtime configuration and version files
dotnet C#, F#, and Visual Basic projects; project and SDK declarations
elixir Elixir and Erlang/OTP; Mix manifests, locks, and tool versions
go Libraries and services; modules and toolchain declarations
java Java and Kotlin; Maven, Gradle, and JDK version files
kubernetes Plain manifests, Helm charts, and kustomizations
node JavaScript and TypeScript; applications and libraries; different package managers
node-actions Different host languages; reusable and ordinary workflows
php Framework applications and Composer libraries; runtime and package declarations
python Applications and libraries; requirements, project manifests, and runtime files
ruby Applications and gems; runtime pins and dependency declarations
rust Applications, libraries, and workspaces; Cargo and toolchain declarations
scala Scala and sbt; build and version declarations
serverless Serverless Framework, SAM, and supported Terraform cloud functions
shell PowerShell scripts, modules, and CI containers
swift Swift packages and Xcode applications; project and toolchain declarations
terraform Modules and deployments; different supported providers

For each bucket, declare strata before selection using supported input forms or stack families from the table, plus small (at most 5,000 KB) and medium (5,001–50,000 KB) repositories. Walk nonempty strata round-robin in a recorded order; within each, sort by lowercase owner/name. Deduplicate overlapping strata. Search for input filenames or ecosystem structure, not deprecated versions or known findings. Record application/library and maintainer diversity where applicable; publish empty strata and search limits rather than inventing coverage.

Never choose the next repository by its score or stop a batch because enough positive or zero-finding examples have appeared. Version-specific searches and known migrations are targeted supplements, labeled targeted and reported separately; they cannot replace the blind sample. Existing blind labels retain their historical meaning under decision 0013, even when their older selection rules differ from this record.

3. Interpret 200 as reviewed projects per bucket

The growth target is 200 distinct eligible upstream repositories in each of the 23 buckets: 4,600 bucket memberships, not 200 overall, 200 findings, or 200 successful scans. A project belongs to one primary bucket chosen from its input evidence before scanning; multiple commits, monorepo packages, or incidental findings from other detectors do not increase the count. All detectors still scan the selected tree, and every judged finding is labeled. Report cross-ecosystem detector evidence separately from bucket membership.

Count an entry toward 200 only after its pin, eligibility, selection provenance, and ground truth have been reviewed, including a review supporting an empty expected list. Retained historical entries count only where their recorded evidence establishes eligibility at their selection date; missing evidence is not grandfathered into the new total. Publish blind and targeted counts alongside the total, and keep at least two thirds of the counted repositories blind, matching the stable selection floor in decision 0013. Reaching 200 alone grants neither stable maturity nor a claim of representative accuracy; the other maturity and independent-validation requirements remain in force, and held-out repositories stay separate from this growth count.

Poor precision, poor recall, unexpected findings, zero findings, parser failures, and slow scans are never reasons to remove or replace a selected repository. Keep failures visible and fix Offing or track the gap. A pending review or failed scan is reported explicitly, not converted into a clean result. Correct wrong labels only with independent evidence and a reviewed history of the correction. Removal requires an objective reason such as a duplicate upstream, lost access, or a confirmed licensing problem, recorded in review with the old pin and reason retained; its replacement follows the same precommitted selection order.

4. Publish an honest shortfall

If the recorded searches and strata cannot supply 200 eligible, reviewed repositories, publish the actual count as N/200, the blind/targeted split, pending reviews and fetch failures, empty strata, discovery date, queries and search limits, and skip reasons. A capped search is evidence of a limited search, not proof that the ecosystem has no more repositories. State which limitation prevents further growth.

Do not pad the count with forks, duplicate commits, fixtures, generated toy projects, other ecosystems, or unreviewed labels; do not relax activity, size, licensing, or blind-selection rules just to hit 200. A maintainer may accept a documented shortfall for the release while the target remains unmet. Any different target or eligibility exception needs a separate reviewed decision before new selection, with its effect on comparability explained. Schedule a follow-up discovery batch when the candidate pool or tooling improves.

Consequences

  • Growth is reproducible from saved selection records and pins; new selection and labeling tooling follows this policy in the remaining tasks of #1993. This record adds no runtime behavior, network path, or dependency.
  • Blind selection remains distinct from independent ground truth. A regression corpus labeled after seeing Offing's output cannot establish generalization; preserve the separate held-out process in Validation corpus.
  • Maintainer merge of the pull request for #2116 records acceptance of this policy. Automated checks establish repository health; they do not supply maintainer acceptance or prove that the corpus already meets it.
